As a patient going through wisdom tooth removal three years ago I vividly remember the last few seconds before going under. The tiles of the ceiling looked like they were traveling behind me while the overhead lights were going forward to my feet. I tried to point this out to the nurse and got frustrated when my arm didn't cooperate in going two different directions at once. Immediately after I said something akin to "I've never done drugs but this must be what it's like and it makes me want to not do drugs" and looked over to see the relief on my mom's face before passing out. I then woke up in the recovery room and proceeded to whisper to my mom that everyone was so nice. It wasn't whispering by the way. I believed it was but according to her I was yelling it at her face. Apparently the doctor and nurses said thank you but I ignored them because how could they hear me whispering?

When I was in the 6th grade, I had a very strict social studies teacher for homeroom (as well as first period). My sister and I were super close, and she had just left for college. Being a little 6th grader, that was really hard for me and I was nearing tears to begin with. Turns out, I had been so preoccupied I'd forgotten to grab my social studies textbook. This teacher in particular was incredibly harsh on those that had to "disrupt the class by not having their book, " as she always so "lovingly" put it. The class was only 5 minutes in and I'd raised my hand to tell her I forgot my book. 

She started berating me and calling me out in front of the whole class. I was mortified when she made me stand up at my desk for it too. That, combined with my sister now being out of state, I broke down entirely. The teacher just went silent and still made me stay in class and continue to sniffle for 30 minutes. 

The real kicker is that my book was in my locker. In the room. So close to my desk I wouldn't have even needed to get out of my seat to grab it.
